title: There’s a man in Scripture who never had a funeral.
paragraphs: There’s a man in Scripture who never had a funeral.

No grave.
No mourning crowd.
No final words.
One day he was here—walking, breathing, living like everyone else. And then… he wasn’t.
The mystery sits quietly in Genesis 5:24: “Enoch walked with God; then he was no more, because God took him.”
Read that again.
He walked with God… and then disappeared.
No explanation. No warning. Just gone.
But here’s what most people don’t realize…

Enoch didn’t vanish because he was extraordinary in the way the world measures greatness. He wasn’t a king. He didn’t build an empire. He didn’t lead armies. His life is summarized in a single phrase that most people skip past without thinking.
He walked with God.
That’s it.
And yet somehow, that was enough to separate him from every other man in his generation.
Because while everyone else was building lives without God… Enoch was moving step by step with Him.
And you know what that means.

It wasn’t a one-time prayer.
It wasn’t occasional religion.
It wasn’t showing up when it was convenient.
Walking implies direction. Consistency. Intimacy.
It means agreement.
Scripture asks in Amos 3:3, “Can two walk together, except they be agreed?”
Enoch didn’t just believe in God. He aligned with Him.
And that’s where the tension starts pressing in.
Because if walking with God requires agreement… then something in you has to die.

Your pride.
Your hidden sin.
Your private compromises.
God saw it.
You knew.

Enoch lived in a time that looked eerily similar to ours—growing corruption, quiet rebellion, people doing what felt right in their own eyes. And in the middle of that noise, he chose a different rhythm.

Step by step.
Day by day.
He walked with God.
Not perfectly—but faithfully.
And something began to happen in that walk.

The more he moved with God, the less he fit in with the world. The closer he got to God’s heart, the more distant everything else became. What once mattered started to feel empty. What once satisfied began to lose its grip.
You’ve felt that before, haven’t you?
That quiet pull.
That inner discomfort when you know you’re not where you should be.
That tension between who you are… and who God is calling you to become.
Enoch didn’t ignore that tension.
He leaned into it.
Hebrews 11:5 reveals something deeper: “By faith Enoch was taken from this life, so that he did not experience death… for before he was taken, he was commended as one who pleased God.”
He pleased God.

Not impressed people.
Not gained followers.
Not built a name.
He pleased God.
And that’s the part that cuts.
Because most people today aren’t walking with God—they’re negotiating with Him.

They want His blessings without His presence.
His promises without His authority.
His grace without repentance.
But Enoch didn’t walk beside God while holding onto sin behind his back.
He surrendered.
And here’s where it becomes unsettling.
Because one day, without warning, God simply took him.
No delay. No explanation.
Just intimacy reaching its full conclusion.
And it forces a question most people avoid:
If God took those who truly walked with Him today… would you still be here?
Let that sit.
Because this isn’t just a mysterious story—it’s a mirror.
Enoch’s life exposes the gap between knowing about God… and actually walking with Him.
Jesus later said in Matthew 7:23, “I never knew you; depart from Me.”
Not “you never knew Me.”
“I never knew you.”
That’s relationship language.
Walking language.
The same kind Enoch had.
And here’s the truth most won’t say out loud:
You can attend church, know Scripture, say the right words—and still not be walking with God.
Because walking with God demands repentance.
It demands surrender.
It demands faith in Jesus Christ—not just as Savior, but as Lord.
Enoch’s story doesn’t end with disappearance. It points forward.
Because one day, there will be another taking.
1 Thessalonians 4:17 says, “Then we who are alive… will be caught up together… to meet the Lord in the air.”
But not everyone goes.
Only those who are His.
Only those who walk with Him.
And suddenly, this ancient mystery becomes personal.
You’re not reading about Enoch anymore.
You’re deciding your own direction.
Because right now, you are walking somewhere.
The question is—with whom?
One path keeps you close to your sin, comfortable, unchallenged… and ultimately separated from God.
The other confronts you, breaks you, reshapes you… and leads you into life.
Through Jesus.
Because this is the Gospel:

You were separated from God by sin.
Christ stepped in, lived perfectly, died in your place, and rose again.
Not to make you religious—but to restore your walk.
Not to improve your image—but to transform your heart.
So you can walk with God again.
Not casually. Not occasionally.
But truly.
If something in you is stirring right now, don’t brush it off.
That conviction—that discomfort—that pull—
That’s not random.
That’s God calling you back to the walk.
Say it plainly if you feel it: “I don’t want to just believe—I want to walk with God.”
Let that be real.
Follow this path if you’re ready to go deeper, to be corrected, sharpened, and anchored in truth.
And if you’re done playing distance with God… step into the walk.
Originally written by Gospel Warrior
